title: Service software increases duplicate work
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: 19 staff; service management software introduced eight months ago.
owner_narrative: The office creates tickets then messages technicians because chat gets noticed. Updates return by chat and are copied back. Long mobile forms and poor connectivity push reporting into the evening. Management asks for separate Excel totals because the dashboard is incomplete.

diagnostic_interview.question: Which fields prevent completion?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Several mandatory fields do not apply to simple jobs.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Workflow configuration may be the obstacle.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: If essential features genuinely cannot be configured or integrated, replacement may be justified after a bounded trial; do not assume another app is always wrong.

evidence.description: A simulated observation records duplicate entry in chat and the app.
A simulated form contains irrelevant mandatory fields.
A simulated dashboard differs from the later reconciled list.

diagnoses.hypothesis: The configured workflow does not fit field conditions and management maintains a competing source of truth.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: If essential features genuinely cannot be configured or integrated, replacement may be justified after a bounded trial; do not assume another app is always wrong.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Observe actual work; remove unjustified fields; define one authoritative queue and reconcile exceptions before retiring the shadow sheet.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: First configure existing software; add reliable notifications and offline draft synchronization only where supported and needed.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: A minimal simple-job form can be submitted without irrelevant data.
Reconnection does not create duplicate jobs.
Conflicting edits appear for resolution rather than overwriting silently.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Offline synchronization may require vendor support; configuration-first intervention precedes a new product.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Duplicate-entry minutes per job and reporting completeness; track sync failures and staff adoption.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Observe actual work; remove unjustified fields; define one authoritative queue and reconcile exceptions before retiring the shadow sheet. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: If essential features genuinely cannot be configured or integrated, replacement may be justified after a bounded trial; do not assume another app is always wrong.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Existing software configuration and API/offline support must be tested before proposing custom development.
